owner: RI-CMB02 §D.3 (root motion is authoritative), RI-CMB01 §C.5, RI-CMB04 §A step 4
units: rotations are Euler XYZ in DEGREES in the bone's local frame; root_forward is a CUMULATIVE FRACTION of the move's declared displacement; root_offset is metres in the character's local frame

phase_parameterisation.why: A clip is authored ONCE as a set of normalised phase curves and INSTANTIATED at each move's own declared frame counts. That keeps the frame data (frames.json / roll.json) the single source of timing while letting the pose be authored where it is legible.
phase_parameterisation.interpolation: smoothstep (3u^2 - 2u^3) between adjacent keys, clamped outside the key range. Deterministic, allocation-free, and NON-LINEAR, which is what makes the per-frame root delta a speed curve rather than a translate (RI-CMB01 M3, RI-CMB02 M3).
phase_parameterisation.not_a_reskin: RI-CMB02's automatic-fail list forbids 'a single attack animation shared by all weapon classes with the numbers swapped'. Classes therefore select DIFFERENT pose archetypes (cut_diagonal / thrust / chop_overhead / sweep_wide), with per-class amplitude and stance, on top of their own frame counts. The archetype assignment is in each moveset file.
phase_parameterisation.termination_rule: BINDING. Every non-looping archetype whose clip can be followed by free locomotion must have, at phase 3.0, exactly the value the `idle_ready` stance layer holds for that bone (0 where idle_ready is silent). The attack/idle boundary is then continuous by construction. Before this rule, a straight-sword R1 moved its tip 1.42 m and a halberd R1 2.54 m in the single frame the move retired — 85 to 152 m/s of pose discontinuity, W1-09 verdict §2.5.

cut_diagonal.note: Authored from corpus/70-visual/refs/souls-behaviour/anim/attacks/er-ER_Moveset_Neutral_Attack_Chain_Longsword.gif (81 frames, 14.286 fps, MANIFEST record). What that clip shows and what this curve now reproduces: the blade drops back and down behind the right hip, rises to an overhead cock with the torso rotated away and the weight on the back foot, and the cut is a DIAGONAL arc through the centreline led by the hips. The recovery is a short follow-through that DECELERATES onto the ready pose — the reference clip's own per-frame motion energy decays monotonically to its resting baseline over the last third of the animation and ends at rest, which the previous curve did not: it over-rotated to a peak at phase 2.4 and then snapped back.
cut_diagonal.solved_note: The pose on the last STARTUP frame is cock + 0.637 x (hit - cock); the active band then runs to `hit` in four evenly spaced keys, and the recovery decelerates onto the idle pose. `t` is solved by tools/harness/anim-author.mjs as the SMALLEST blend at which every class using this archetype measures a peak tip speed at or under its RI-CMB04 §B declared column with a 4 % margin — smallest, so that as much of the arc as possible is inside the hitbox-active window rather than hidden in the windup.

chop_overhead.note: Axe. Authored against ds1-boss-moves/Gargoyle-Smash.gif and Artorias_-_Heavy_Slam.gif: the head is raised straight over the shoulder, held, and driven down the centreline with almost no torso twist, and the settle is LONG — the head buries low and the body is pulled back off it. The settle is now authored as a deceleration onto the ready pose rather than a second excursion.
chop_overhead.solved_note: The pose on the last STARTUP frame is cock + 0.407 x (hit - cock); the active band then runs to `hit` in four evenly spaced keys, and the recovery decelerates onto the idle pose. `t` is solved by tools/harness/anim-author.mjs as the SMALLEST blend at which every class using this archetype measures a peak tip speed at or under its RI-CMB04 §B declared column with a 4 % margin — smallest, so that as much of the arc as possible is inside the hitbox-active window rather than hidden in the windup.

thrust.note: Spear and dagger. Authored against ds1-boss-moves/Ornstein-Thrust.gif and Kings-Thrust.gif: the weapon is chambered beside the hip with the point already on line, the body drops into a lunge, and the whole displacement is LINEAR along the point. Almost no arc — which is exactly why a spear's swept volume is a narrow tube and why stepping 20 cm sideways beats it. The recovery pulls the point back off line and settles on the ready pose.

sweep_wide.note: Halberd. Authored against ds1-boss-moves/Kings-Horizontal.gif and Golem-Side-Slash.gif: drawn to the right rear at shoulder height and swept HORIZONTALLY across the front arc. The old curve over-rotated PAST the target and then unwound, which is how a 108-frame R1 came to sweep 665° at 59.1 m/s. It now arrives on line as the hitbox opens, carries through the arc at a bounded rate, and unwinds onto the ready pose.

roll_ground.note: Authored from corpus/70-visual/refs/souls-behaviour/anim/stance/er-ER_Skill_Quickstep_Forward.gif (31 frames). What that clip shows: the displacement is strongly FRONT-LOADED — the character crouches, covers most of the ground in the first third, and the tail is a stationary RISE with no translation at all. The root_forward curve below reaches 1.00 at phase 2.55, which is the last frame of the HARD sub-phase (f42 on a LIGHT roll), so the TURN sub-phase RI-CMB09 §2 requires to be translation-free is exactly that.

backstep.note: A short hop straight back with the guard kept up. Much less tuck than a roll, which is why it buys 8 i-frames instead of 26.

parry_sweep.note: The offhand sweeps up and across the incoming line, palm leading. Authored from anim/impact/ds-Parry_Standard.gif (21 frames): the whole motion is in the LEFT arm and the torso barely moves, which is why a parry leaves you standing still and wide open when it misses.

block_hold.note: Shield up, weight back, weapon held low and ready. A held pose, not a motion.

stagger_recoil.note: The torso is driven back off the line of the blow, the guard collapses, the feet chase to catch the weight. Uncancellable by anything, including further hits.

guard_break_open.note: The shield arm is thrown wide and the head comes up — the readable, exploitable tell RI-CMB03 §D exists to make. Deliberately a LARGER excursion than a stagger, so it is identifiable at distance even though it is currently four frames SHORTER (the inversion declared in stamina.json).

crit_thrust.note: Backstab and riposte. The attacker steps in, drops the point and drives it home on the declared damage frame. The long tail is the attacker pulling the weapon back out, and it is where the invulnerability ends and a second enemy kills you.

heal_drink.note: The flask comes up to the face in the right hand and stays there for the whole 62-frame ramp. The weapon hand is occupied, which is the readable reason you cannot answer anything for 130 frames.

parley_open.note: S13. The weapon hand DROPS and the offhand comes up open, palm out, at chest height — the one unmistakable non-combat gesture in the game, held long enough that anything watching can read it. There is no menu, no pause, and no dice: the whole interaction is this animation plus a deterministic test against out-of-fight state.

idle_ready.note: Weapon low and to the side, weight even, guard not raised. The neutral the frame data is measured from.

locomotion_cycle.note: A single walk/run cycle, phase-looped. Only the legs and the counter-swing of the arms; the upper body pose is whatever the stance layer says. Present so the hurtboxes MOVE while walking — a standing character whose hurtboxes never change is the failure RI-CMB04 M1 tests for.

dead_collapse.note: The knees go first. Hurtboxes follow the skeleton into death (RI-CMB04 §D.1), so a corpse is still a shape in the world.

idle_loop.note: The idle BASE loop. A slow breathing/weight-shift cycle and nothing else — no absolute arm pose, because the arms come from the additive stance layer (idle_ready or block_hold). Before this archetype existed, `_idle` played idle_ready AND the stance layer added idle_ready on top, so a standing character held DOUBLE the authored idle pose and every attack clip ended a whole idle pose away from it: the 1.42-2.54 m single-frame weapon snap the W1-09 verdict §2.5 measured at the attack/idle boundary. It still moves every frame, which is the property RI-CMB04 M1 tests for.
